en: 1. Gilgit Manuscript: Ārya-Maitreya-vyākaraṇam, edited by Prabhas Chandra Majumder (1959).
Calcutta (also published in Nalinaksha Dutt, *Gilgit Manuscripts*, vol. IV).
Calcutta 1959, pp. xxix ff. and 185 ff., under P.C. Mazumder.
The first folios of the Sanskrit manuscript containing verses 1–30 are missing. All sandhi rules have been standardized. (daśa māsāṃś ca)
Then, having supported all those of great splendor in this well-flowered garden, the mother of Maitreya [remained there].
Neither sitting nor lying down, that practitioner of the Dharma will give birth to Maitreya while standing, supported by a branch of a tree.
Unstained by the mire of the womb, like a lotus by water,
he will fill this entire triple world with his radiance.
Then the thousand-eyed king of the gods, Śacī’s husband, being pleased,
was to receive that Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds, at the moment of his birth.
As soon as he is born, he will take seven steps;
at every step, there shall be a lotus, one lotus for each step.
Looking toward the four quarters, he will utter these words:
"This is my final birth; there is no further becoming.
I shall not come again; I shall pass away, free from outflows."
For those beings submerged in the ocean of saṃsāra,
who partake in suffering and are bound by the fetters of craving, I shall effect their liberation.
The gods shall hold a white parasol over his head,
and two lords of the nāgas shall bathe him with streams of cold and warm water.
And having received him, who possesses the thirty-two excellent marks and blazes with splendor, the nurse will present Maitreya to his mother.
And the deities shall carry her, who has ascended a beautiful palanquin adorned with various jewels, together with her son.
Then, as thousands of musical instruments are being played,
as soon as Maitreya enters that city, a rain of flowers will fall.
Having thus seen his son endowed with the thirty-two excellent marks, Subrahmā will then look back upon the mantras and become joyful.
Two destinies for the prince are seen in the mantras:
he shall be either a universal monarch, a lord of men, or a Buddha, the supreme among the best of bipeds.
And when that Maitreya, the supreme among men and whose nature is dharma, has reached his youth, he will reflect: "Alas, these living beings are indeed suffering."
With a voice like that of Brahmā, a great resonance, the color of gold, and great splendor;
broad-chested, with full shoulders, and eyes resembling lotus petals.
The height of his body will be fifty cubits, and its breadth shall be half of that; he will possess a sublime form of beautiful complexion.
Surrounded by eighty-four thousand young brahmins,
that Maitreya will teach them the mantras.
Then King Śaṅkha will cause a sacrificial pillar to be erected,
sixteen fathoms in width and one thousand fathoms in height.
Having performed a sacrifice preceded by all preliminary rites, that lord of men will bestow upon the twice-born that sacrificial post adorned with various jewels;
he will give that sacrificial post made of the seven precious gems to the brahmins.
And as soon as that delightful sacrificial post made of jewels is given away,
thousands of brahmins will scatter it in that very instant.
Having seen this impermanence of that sacrificial post and having reflected upon the entirety of saṃsāra, Maitreya will take delight in the life of a renunciant.
So that, having gone forth here, I may touch the deathless state and liberate the people from the fear of disease, death, and old age.
Honored by eighty-four thousand followers,
Maitreya, the foremost of persons, will go forth into the homeless life.
At that time, the Nāga tree will become his Bodhi tree;
its branches will rise fifty yojanas high.
And having sat down beneath it, Maitreya, the Supreme Person and Leader,
will attain unsurpassed, auspicious enlightenment.
On the very night that he shall go forth into the homeless life,
on that same night he will indeed attain supreme enlightenment.
Then that Supreme among Men will teach the True Dharma, which removes all suffering and is auspicious, with speech endowed with the eight qualities.
Seeing the people with serene minds, he will proclaim the truths:
suffering, the origin of suffering, and the transcendence of suffering.
And having heard that noble eightfold path, which leads to security and Nirvana,
they will also practice that Dharma within the teaching.
In a garden covered with flowers, there will be an assembly;
his retinue will fill a full hundred yojanas.
Having heard this, the king, the lord of men named Śaṅkha of great renown,
will give incalculable gifts and go forth into the homeless life.
Surrounded by eighty-four thousand [attendants],
the lord of men, having gone forth, will enter the religious life.
By this very measure,
the father of Maitreya, honored by men, will go forth into homelessness there.
Then, there will be a renowned householder named Sudhana;
pure in soul, he will go forth into homelessness under the instruction of Maitreya.
Then, the jewel among women of Śaṅkha, renowned by the name Viśākhā,
surrounded by eighty-four thousand [attendants],
will go forth from her home and take delight in the religious life.
At that time, hundreds and thousands of living beings will go forth into the homeless life under the instruction of Maitreya.
In this well-flowered garden there will be a great assembly;
his retinue will extend for a hundred yojanas in every direction.
Then the compassionate Teacher, Maitreya, the Supreme among Men,
having surveyed the assembly, will proclaim this matter.

All of them have been seen by the Lion of the Śākyas, the supreme among the virtuous, the Protector, the Lord of the World in its true sense; having been established on the path to liberation by means of the realm of the True Dharma, they have been scattered throughout my teaching.
Having rendered honor to the stūpas with parasols, banners, and flags, and with perfumes, garlands, and ointments, they have indeed come into my presence.
Having given gifts to the Saṅgha— robes, food and drink,
and various medicines for the sick— they have indeed come into my presence.
Having offered a sprinkling of saffron water and an anointing with sandalwood paste at the stūpas of Śākyamuni, they have indeed come into my presence.
Having undertaken the precepts within the teaching of the Lion of the Śākyas and having observed them correctly as they truly are, they have indeed come into my presence.
Having observed here the noble and auspicious eightfold *upoṣadha* on the fourteenth,
the fifteenth, and likewise the eighth day of the fortnight,
as well as during the fortnight of miracles, being well-composed in the eightfold [vow].
Having undertaken the precepts and attained the teaching,
those beings who have gone to the instruction of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha,
and having performed wholesome karma, have come to my teaching.
Therefore, these beings were sent by him, and they have been accepted by me as well;
they are encompassed by the Sage, the best of leaders, who possesses vast wisdom.
Seeing that the people have become serene, he will proclaim the truths;
and having heard the Dharma from him, they will attain the supreme state.
By means of the three miracles, he will discipline the disciples;
all those gentle ones will there exhaust their outflows.
His first assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-six billion followers who have severed the cycle of existence.
His second assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-four full koṭis of those who are peaceful and of vast intelligence.
His third assembly of disciples will consist of twenty-two full koṭis of those who are peaceful and whose minds are tranquil.
Then, having set in motion the wheel of Dharma and having disciplined gods and humans,
he will wander for alms in the city together with the community of disciples.
Then, as he enters that delightful city of Ketumatī,
celestial flowers of the māndāraka variety will fall upon that supreme city;
for when the Sage has arrived in the city, the deities will scatter them there.
The four great kings and Śakra, lord of the thirty-three gods,
together with Brahmā and the hosts of deities, shall perform worship for him.
Blue lotuses, white water-lilies, red lotuses, white lotuses, and fragrant flowers,
as well as aloe-wood, sandalwood, and divine garlands will fall down.
The sons of the gods, possessed of great supernatural power,
will cast their garments as they gaze upon that Lord of the World entering the supreme city.
And a divine sound of musical instruments and divine garlands will fall;
the deities will scatter them when the Sage has entered that city.
And those humans who shall dwell in Ketumatī will also pay homage to him as he enters that supreme city.
Then, upon that path, they will scatter a soft ground-covering like cotton-wool, as well as various beautiful garlands.
With parasols, banners, and flags, humans shall worship [him],
and with the auspicious sounds of musical instruments, men whose minds are serene.
And Śakra, the thousand-eyed king of the gods and husband of Śacī,
being greatly delighted and with palms joined in reverence, shall praise the Jina Maitreya.
Homage to you, O noble among men; homage to you, O supreme among men.
Have compassion for the people, O Blessed One, O foremost of persons.
A son of the gods possessed of great supernatural power will become his Māra;
and he too, with palms joined in reverence, will praise the Leader of the World.
Surrounded by many thousands of Śuddhāvāsa deities, Maitreya, the Lord of the World and Guide, will enter [the city].
Surrounded by a retinue of Brahmās, Brahmā himself will also proclaim the true Dharma with clear words, uttering a Brahmā-like voice.
The entire earth will be filled with Arhats—
those whose taints are exhausted, who have vomited out their faults, and who have severed the bonds of existence.
Delighted gods and humans, gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas,
as well as nāgas of great supernatural power, will perform worship for the Teacher.
They will surely become free from sin,
with their accumulations severed;
wise ones who have filled in the moat, who grasp nothing, and who are devoid of longing.
They will practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
They too will surely be without "mine-ness" and without possessions;
they will be without gold or silver, without fixed dwellings, and free from social attachments— those who shall practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
Having cut through the very net of worldly existence with their own arms, they will indeed go to the realm of the gods;
and having attained the meditative absorptions (dhyānas), endowed with joy and bliss,
they will practice the holy life (brahmacarya) under the instruction of Maitreya.
For sixty thousand years, Maitreya, the best of bipeds and the Teacher, will proclaim the true Dharma out of compassion for the world.
Having disciplined hundreds and thousands of living beings through his Dharma-body, that Guide will then proceed to nirvāṇa.
And when that wise Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds, has entered parinirvāṇa,
the True Dharma will remain upon the earth for ten thousand years.
Therefore, you shall gladden your hearts toward the Jina Śākyamuni;
thereafter, you will behold Maitreya, the perfectly awakened one, the supreme among bipeds.
Therefore, by gladdening the mind toward the Dharma, the Buddha, and the Sangha, the supreme assembly, one will possess great supernatural power.
Having propitiated that compassionate Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds,
at the proper time, you shall thereafter attain nirvāṇa.
Having heard this marvel and seen such no small splendor,
what wise person would not be filled with faith, even among those born into dark births?
Therefore, in this world, one who desires their own welfare and aspires to greatness should hold the true Dharma in high esteem, keeping the Buddha’s teaching in mind.
The Prophecy of Maitreya is completed.

2. Calcutta Manuscript (incomplete), edited by Sylvain Lévi, “Maitreya le consolateur,” in *Études d’orientalisme publiées par le Musée Guimet à la mémoire de Raymonde Linossier*, Paris 1932, pp. 384–389.
The first two folios of the Sanskrit manuscript containing verses 1–25ab are missing.
All sandhi rules have been standardized.
Elāpattra was in Gāndhāra, and Śaṅkha was in the city of Vārāṇasī. (MvyC 25)
Endowed with these four treasures, that king will become a great hero, arisen through the power of a hundred merits.
There will be a brahmin, a most excellent brahmin, who is learned and a master of the four Vedas, who shall serve as the domestic priest and preceptor of that king.
He was a teacher who held the mantras, possessed of memory, and had mastered the Vedas;
likewise, he was proficient in the Kaiṭabha, the Nirghaṇṭa, and the science of grammar.
At that time, his wife will be named Brahmāvatī;
she will be beautiful, pleasing, handsome, and renowned.
Having descended from the Tuṣita heaven, Maitreya, the foremost of persons,
will certainly take rebirth in her womb.
Having carried [the fetus] for the full ten months, the mother of Maitreya, endowed with great splendor, went to a garden in full bloom.
Neither sitting nor lying down, that practitioner of the Dharma remains standing,
leaning against a branch of a tree, and will give birth to Maitreya.
The Supreme among Men will go forth by way of the southern side,
shining like the sun emerging from a mass of clouds.
Unstained by the mire of the womb, just as a lotus is unstained by water,
he will fill this entire triple world with his radiance.
Then the thousand-eyed King of the Gods, the Lord of Śacī, being delighted,
will take up that boy as he is born, the most excellent of men.
"O Thousand-eyed One, release, release Maitreya, who blazes with splendor and possesses the thirty-two excellent marks; as soon as he is born, he will speak."
As soon as he is born, he will take seven steps;
at every step, there shall be a treasure, and at every step, a lotus shall appear.
Looking toward the four directions, he will utter these words:
"This is my final birth; there is no further existence."
I shall not return; I shall enter parinirvāṇa, free from outflows.
The nāgas shall bathe me with streams of cold and warm water.
Divine garments and flowers will fall from the expanse of the sky;
the gods will hold a white parasol over his head.
And the thousand-eyed King of the Gods, the Lord of Śacī, being delighted,
will take that youth endowed with the thirty-two excellent marks;
he will place Maitreya, blazing with splendor, into his mother’s hands.
And having ascended a beautiful palanquin adorned with various jewels,
she shall be carried out like a god together with her son.
Then, as thousands of musical instruments are being played,
as soon as Maitreya has entered that city, a rain of flowers will fall.
And on that day, wives who are pregnant shall give birth;
they shall all safely and auspiciously bring forth sons.
And having seen his son, who possesses the thirty-two excellent marks, Subrahmā will examine him in the mantras and thereafter become joyful.
Two destinies for the prince are seen in the prophecies:
he shall be either a sovereign of men, a universal monarch, or a Buddha, the supreme among the best of bipeds.
And when that Maitreya, the foremost of persons, has reached his youth, he, whose nature is the Dharma, will reflect: "Alas, these beings are indeed suffering."
With the voice of Brahmā and a great resonance, golden-hued and of great splendor,
broad-chested and with full-limbed body, his eyes resemble the petals of a lotus.
His body will be eighty cubits in height;
its width will be twenty cubits, and the circle of his face half of that.
Honored by eighty-four thousand young brahmins,
Maitreya will teach them the mantras.
Then the great king Śaṅkha will erect a sacrificial pillar sixteen fathoms in width and one thousand fathoms in height.
Having first performed a sacrifice, that lord of men will bestow upon the twice-born that sacrificial post adorned with various jewels;
he will give to the brahmins a sacrificial post made of the seven precious gems.
And at that very moment, as soon as that beautiful sacrificial pillar made of jewels has been given away, thousands of brahmins will distribute it.
Having seen this impermanence of that sacrificial post and having reflected upon the entirety of saṃsāra, Maitreya will take delight in the life of renunciation.
"Having gone forth here, may I touch the deathless state and liberate the people from the fear of sickness, death, and old age."
Honored by eighty-four thousand followers,
Maitreya, the foremost of persons, will go forth into the homeless life.
At that time, the Nāga tree shall become his Bodhi tree;
its branches will rise fifty yojanas high,
and its boughs will extend six krośas in every direction.
Seated at its base is this Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds;
he shall attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment—of this there is no doubt.
Then that best of sages will teach the true Dharma, which removes all suffering and leads to peace, with speech endowed with the eight excellent qualities.
Suffering, the origin of suffering, the transcendence of suffering,
and the noble eightfold path leading to the security of Nirvāṇa.
Seeing that the people are serene, he will proclaim the truths;
and having heard his Dharma, they will practice according to his teaching.
And in the Supuṣpita garden there will be an assembly;
his retinue will fill a full hundred yojanas.
Then, having heard this, the king Śaṅkha, a monarch of great renown,
will give away incalculable gifts and take delight in the life of renunciation.
Honored by eighty-four thousand [followers],
that lord of men, having gone forth, will enter the religious life.
And by that very same measure,
the father of Maitreya, who is honored among men, will likewise go forth into the homeless life.
Then the householder named Sudhana, renowned and righteous in nature, will go forth into the religious life, surrounded by thousands of followers.
Then the jewel among women of Śaṅkha, renowned by the name Viśākhā,
preceded by eighty-four thousand women, will go forth and enter the religious life.
At that time, hundreds and thousands of living beings will go forth into the homeless life under the instruction of Maitreya.
Then the compassionate Teacher, Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds,
having surveyed the assembly, will proclaim this matter.
All of them have been seen by Śākyamuni, the best of sages, the protector, the Lord of the World, through the essence of the realm of the True Dharma;
they have been established upon the path to liberation and cast into my teaching.
Having performed worship of Śākyamuni with parasols, banners, and flags, as well as perfumes, garlands, and ointments, they have indeed come to my teaching.
Having offered anointment with saffron-water and sandalwood paste at the stūpa of Śākyamuni, they have indeed come to my teaching.
Having always gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha,
and having performed virtuous deeds, they have come into my teaching.
Having undertaken the precepts within the teaching of Śākyamuni and having observed them according to reality, they have indeed come to my teaching.
Having given gifts to the Saṅgha— robes, food and drink,
and various medicines for the sick— they have indeed come to my teaching.
Having observed the fast with the eight limbs well-composed on the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and likewise the eighth day of the fortnight, as well as during the fortnight of miracles,
they have come here to my teaching.
Through the three miracles, he will cause his disciples to realize;
for they shall all exhaust all phenomena associated with the outflows.
His first assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-six billion followers who have severed the cycle of existence.
His second assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-four full koṭis who are liberated from the bonds of the afflictions.
His third assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-two billion who are liberated and whose minds are at peace.
Then, having set in motion the wheel of Dharma and having disciplined gods and humans,
he will wander for alms in the city together with the community of disciples.
Then, as he enters the beautiful city of Ketumatī,
celestial flowers of the māndārava variety will fall upon that best of men;
for when the Sage has entered that city, the deities will scatter them.
The four great kings and Śakra, lord of the thirty-three gods,
together with the hosts of Brahmā deities, will perform worship for him.
Blue lotuses, white water lilies, red lotuses, white lotuses, and fragrant flowers;
likewise, aloe wood, sandalwood, and divine garlands.
The sons of the gods, possessed of great supernatural power, will wave their garments as they gaze upon that Lord of the World entering the supreme city.
On that path, the ground will be situated there, soft like cotton wool;
and they shall spread out various kinds of garlands along the way.
With parasols, banners, and flags, with perfumes, garlands, and ointments,
and with the sounds of musical instruments heard by them, men with serene minds and sons of the gods possessing great supernatural power will perform worship to the Teacher.
And that Śakra, the thousand-eyed king of the gods, possessed of great splendor,
being overjoyed and joining his palms in reverence, shall praise the Leader of the World.
Homage to you, O noble among men; homage to you, O supreme among men.
Have compassion for the people, O Blessed One, O foremost of persons.
A son of the gods possessed of great supernatural power will become his Māra;
and he, with palms joined in reverence, shall praise the Leader of the World.
Surrounded by a retinue of Brahmās and himself placed at their head,
he will proclaim the True Dharma, uttering the voice of Brahmā.
The entire earth will be filled with Arhats—
those whose outflows are exhausted, who have vomited forth their faults, and for whom the bonds of existence have been abandoned.
The gods and humans, the gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, as well as the nāgas of great supernatural power, will all joyfully perform worship for the Teacher.
And they will surely become entirely free from all accumulations,
with the streams of existence severed, without further rebirth, having crossed the ocean of existence;
they will lead the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
They will indeed truly become free from the sense of "mine" and without possessions;
unattached to gold or silver, homeless and without social intimacy, they will practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
They will surely become those whose snares and bonds are severed;
having attained the meditative absorptions (dhyānas) and being endowed with joy and bliss,
they will practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
For sixty thousand years, Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds,
will teach the true Dharma out of compassion for all living beings.
Having disciplined hundreds of thousands of millions of living beings in the true Dharma, that Guide will thereafter enter nirvāṇa.
When that Great Sage has entered final nirvana,
the True Dharma will then remain for ten thousand years.
Having purified your minds toward that Victor Śākyamuni,
you shall then behold Maitreya, the perfectly awakened one, the supreme among bipeds.
Having heard of this marvel and this unsurpassed supernatural power,
what wise person— even one of the most dark birth— would not be filled with faith?
Therefore, one who desires their own welfare here and aspires to greatness should hold the true Dharma in high esteem, remembering the teaching of the Buddha.
The Prophecy of Maitreya is completed.
Of those phenomena which [arise from causes]... [etc. //

Whatever merit is herein from the monk Puṇyakīrti, who has come forth from the land of China, may that merit, placing his teachers, preceptors, mother, and father foremost, be for the attainment of the fruit of unsurpassed knowledge by the entire mass of sentient beings.
In the year 57 of the reign of the illustrious King Gopāla, on the ninth day of the month of Phālguna, [this was] written in the village of Ghosalī:
Oṃ Hārītī, Great Yakṣiṇī, take away, take away all my sins, svāhā!

Oṃ, homage to the Lord Maitreya!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha, in the Bamboo Grove, at the Kalandaka Feeding Ground, together with a great community of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty monks.
Then indeed, the venerable Śāriputra, the great wise one, the commander of the Dharma, the all-pervading lord, questioned the Teacher for the sake of compassion for the world.
That future Buddha who has been described as the Leader of the World,
he is known by the name Maitreya in the *Sūtra-pūrvāparāntika*.
O Leader, I wish to hear its detailed account;
O Best of Men, tell me of its supernatural power and its majesty.
Then the Teacher said to him: "I shall explain it to you;
listen to me concerning that Buddha Maitreya in detail."
At that time, the ocean, measuring thirty-two hundred yojanas,
will be dried up, just as this [present] universal monarch [dries up the waters].
Jambudvīpa will be ten thousand yojanas in extent,
a vast abode for all beings on every side.
At that time, there will be people who perform virtuous deeds, in lands flourishing with miraculous powers, free from punishment and free from calamity.
The earth was free from thorns and covered with lush, green grass;
rising and falling, it was as soft as a tuft of cotton wool.
Rice will grow without being sown, fragrant and sweet as honey;
there will be trees that yield garments, adorned with various colors.
The trees, laden with flowers, leaves, and fruits, will rise to a height of one krośa;
their lifespan will be eighty thousand years.
And those beings were free from disease, devoid of sorrow, and full of great joy;
they were endowed with beautiful complexions, possessed of great majesty, and filled with the strength of mighty elephants.
There will be three diseases: desire, hunger, and old age;
a maiden of five hundred years shall choose her husband.
At that time, there will be a royal capital named Ketumatī,
a dwelling for pure beings and for living creatures who perform virtuous deeds.
A delightful city, twelve yojanas in length and seven yojanas in breadth, will belong to those who have performed meritorious deeds.
The ramparts made of the seven precious gems were one krośa in height;
the bricks and door-panels were adorned with various kinds of jewels.
And there will be assemblies, constructed with precious bricks,
strewn with lotuses and water-lilies, and adorned with ruddy geese.
Surrounded on all sides by seven rows of palm trees,
those palms consist of the four jewels and are adorned with networks of tinkling bells.
Then, from the palm trees shaken by the wind, auspicious sounds will arise, enchanting to the ear, like the music of five-fold orchestral instruments.
And those mortals in that city who were endowed with the pleasure of sporting and delight shall,
being filled with joy, sport by means of that very sound of the *tāla*.
There will be lotus ponds filled with white and blue water-lilies,
and that city will be endowed with gardens and groves.
Then there will be a king named Śaṅkha, of great splendor,
a powerful universal monarch (cakravartin) and lord of the four continents.
Endowed with a fourfold army and possessed of the seven jewels,
that king will have a full thousand sons.
That lord of men shall protect this earth, bounded by the ocean, through righteousness and impartiality, without the use of force.
At that time, there will be four great treasures, numbering hundreds of millions of nayutas, belonging to that King Śaṅkha, the lord of the earth.
Piṅgala was among the Kaliṅgas, Pāṇḍuka in Mithilā,
Elāpatra in Gāndhāra, and Śaṅkha in the city of Vārāṇasī.
Endowed with these four treasures, that great hero, bestowed with the fruit of a hundred merits, shall become a king.
Then, there will be a brahmin named Subrahmā who, being deeply learned and a master of the four Vedas, will serve as that king's domestic priest and preceptor.
He was a teacher who held the mantras in memory, possessed of traditional knowledge, and had mastered the Vedas;
likewise, he was proficient in the Kaiṭabha, the Nirghaṇṭu, and the science of grammar.
At that time, his wife will be named Brahmavatī;
she will be beautiful, pleasing, handsome, and renowned.
Then, having passed away from the Tuṣita heaven, Maitreya, the foremost of persons,
will certainly take rebirth in her womb.
Having carried the one of great splendor for the full ten months,
the mother of Maitreya went to a garden in full bloom.
Neither sitting nor lying down, that woman practicing the holy life will give birth to Maitreya while standing, supported by a branch of a tree.
The Supreme among Men will emerge from his right side,
shining forth like the sun emerging from a mass of clouds.
Honored by humans and gods alike, he will bring forth illumination;
unstained by the mire of the womb, just like a lotus by water,
he will fill this entire triple world with his radiance.
At every step there shall be a treasure and a lotus after lotus;
looking toward the four directions, he will utter these words:
"This is my final birth; there is no further becoming."
I shall not return again; I shall enter parinirvāṇa, free from outflows.
The nāgas shall bathe me with streams of cold and warm water.
Divine and celestial flowers will fall from the vault of the sky;
the gods will hold a white parasol over his head.
And the thousand-eyed one, the king of the gods and husband of Śacī, being delighted,
will take that prince endowed with the thirty-two marks;
he will place Maitreya, blazing with splendor, into his mother’s hand.
And the deities shall carry the beautiful palanquin, adorned with various jewels, upon which she has ascended together with her son.
Then, as thousands of musical instruments are being played,
as soon as Maitreya has entered that city, a rain of flowers will fall.
And on that day, pregnant women shall give birth;
they shall all safely and auspiciously bring forth sons.
Having thus seen his son, who possesses the thirty-two excellent marks, Subrahmā will then become joyful after reflecting upon him with Sumantra.
Two destinies for the prince are seen in the mantras:
he shall become either a sovereign of men, a universal monarch, or a Buddha, the supreme among the best of bipeds.
And when that Maitreya, the foremost person, has attained youth, he, whose nature is the Dharma, will reflect: "Alas, these living beings are indeed suffering."
With the voice of Brahmā, great speed, golden complexion, and immense luster;
with wide eyes and full limbs, his gaze was like the opening petals of a lotus.
The height of his body will be eighty cubits;
its width will be twenty cubits, and the circle of his face half of that.
Honored by eighty-four thousand young brahmins,
that Maitreya will teach them the sacred mantras.
Then the great king Śaṅkha will erect a sacrificial pillar sixteen vyāmas in width and one thousand vyāmas in height.
That lord of men will bestow upon the brahmins that sacrificial pillar, adorned with various jewels and strewn with the seven precious gems.
And as soon as that delightful sacrificial pillar made of jewels is given away,
thousands of brahmins will instantly divide it among themselves.
Having seen this impermanence of that sacrificial post and having reflected upon the entirety of saṃsāra, Maitreya will take delight in the life of renunciation.
So that, having gone forth here, I may touch the deathless state and liberate the people from the fear of sickness, death, and old age.
Surrounded by eighty-four thousand followers,
Maitreya, the foremost of persons, will go forth for the sake of renunciation.
Then the Nāga tree will become his Bodhi tree;
its branches will extend fifty yojanas upward,
and its foliage and boughs will spread for six krośas in every direction.
Seated at its base is this Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds;
he shall attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment—of this there is no doubt.
Then that Supreme Person will teach the true Dharma, which removes all suffering and brings auspiciousness, with speech endowed with the eight qualities.
Suffering, the origin of suffering, the transcendence of suffering,
and the noble eightfold path leading to the security of Nirvana.
Seeing the people with serene minds, he will proclaim the Truths;
and having heard his Dharma in such a way, they will practice within the Teaching.
And in the Supuṣpita grove there will be a gathering;
his assembly will be a full hundred yojanas in extent.
Then, having heard this, the king named Śaṅkha, of great renown,
will give incalculable gifts and take delight in the life of renunciation.
Honored by eighty-four thousand [followers],
that lord of men, having gone forth, will likewise enter the religious life.
And by that very same measure,
the father of Maitreya, who is honored among men, will likewise go forth into the homeless life.
Then, there will be a renowned householder named Sudhana;
that righteous soul will go forth into homelessness, surrounded by thousands.
Then, the jewel among women of Śaṅkha, renowned by the name Viśākhā,
preceded by eighty-four thousand women, will go forth and enter the religious life.
At that time, hundreds and thousands of living beings will go forth into the religious life under the instruction of Maitreya.
Then the compassionate Teacher, Maitreya, the supreme among bipeds,
having surveyed the assembly, shall proclaim this matter.
All of them were seen in their true sense by Śākyamuni, the best of sages, the protector, the Lord of the World, through the realm of the True Dharma;
they were established on the path to liberation and placed within my teaching.
Having performed worship of Śākyamuni with umbrellas, banners, and flags, as well as perfumes, garlands, and ointments, they have indeed come into my teaching.
Having offered a sprinkling of saffron water and an anointing with sandalwood paste at the stūpa of Śākyamuni, they have indeed come into my teaching.
Having always gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha,
and having performed wholesome deeds, they have indeed come to my teaching.
Having undertaken the precepts in the teaching of the Lion of the Śākyas and having practiced them according to reality, they have indeed come to my teaching.
Having given gifts to the Saṅgha— robes, food and drink,
and various medicines for the sick— they have indeed come to my teaching.
Having observed the fast with the eight limbs here, well-composed on the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and likewise the eighth day of the fortnight, as well as during the fortnight of miracles,
they have come here unto my teaching.
Through the three miracles, he will discipline the disciples;
all those well-behaved ones will bring the out-flowing phenomena to an end.
His first assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-six full koṭis of śrāvakas.
His second assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-four full koṭis who, in a single moment, will be liberated from the afflictions.
His third assembly of disciples will consist of ninety-two billion who are liberated and whose minds are at peace.
Then, having set in motion the wheel of Dharma and having disciplined gods and humans,
he will wander for alms in the city together with the community of disciples.
Then, as he enters the beautiful city of Ketumatī,
Māndārava flowers will fall upon that supreme city;
the deities will proceed [to honor him] when the Sage has entered that city.
The four great kings and Śakra, lord of the thirty-three gods,
together with Brahmā and the hosts of deities, shall perform worship for him.
The blue lotus, the white water-lily, the red lotus, the white lotus, and the fragrant flower;
likewise, aloe-wood, sandalwood, and divine garlands.
The sons of the gods, possessing great supernatural power,
will cast their garments as they gaze upon that Lord of the World entering the supreme city.
The ground situated along that path will be soft like cotton wool,
and they will scatter various kinds of garlands upon the path.
With parasols, banners, and flags; with perfumes, garlands, and ointments;
and with the auspicious sounds of musical instruments, men of serene minds and sons of the gods possessed of great supernatural power will perform worship to the Teacher.
And Śakra, the thousand-eyed king of the gods, possessed of great splendor,
being overjoyed and joining his palms in reverence, shall praise the Leader of the World.
Homage to you, O lion among men; homage to you, O supreme among men.
Have compassion for the people, O Blessed One, O foremost of persons.
A son of the gods possessed of great supernatural power will become his Māra;
and he, with palms joined in reverence, shall praise the Leader of the World.
Surrounded by many thousands of Śuddhāvāsa deities,
Maitreya, the delighter of the world, will enter Ketumatī.
Surrounded by a retinue of Brahmās and himself placed at their head,
he will proclaim the True Dharma, uttering the Brahma-voice.
The entire earth will be filled with Arhats—
those whose taints are exhausted, who have vomited out faults, and who have severed the bonds of existence.
The gods and humans, the gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, as well as the nāgas of great supernatural power, will all be joyful and perform worship to the Teacher.
They will surely become entirely free from doubt;
with the stream of existence severed and grasping at nothing, they will have crossed over the ocean of existence and will practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
They will indeed truly become free from the sense of "mine" and without possessions;
unattached to gold or silver, homeless and without rebirth, they will practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
They will surely become those whose snares are severed and who are free from power;
having attained the meditative absorptions, endowed with joy and bliss,
they will practice the holy life under the instruction of Maitreya.
For sixty thousand years, Maitreya, the best of bipeds and compassionate toward all beings, will teach the true Dharma.
Having disciplined hundreds of thousands of millions of living beings in the true Dharma, that leader will then attain nirvana.
When that very great sage Maitreya has entered parinirvāṇa,
the True Dharma will then remain for ten thousand years.
You shall gladden your minds toward that Victor Śākyamuni;
thereafter, you shall behold Maitreya, the perfectly awakened one, the supreme among bipeds.
Having heard of this marvel and this unsurpassed supernatural power,
what wise person— even one of lowly birth— would not be filled with faith?
Therefore, one who desires their own welfare here and aspires to greatness,
remembering the teaching of the Buddha, should hold the true Dharma in high esteem.

Thus ends the Mahāyāna sūtra titled "The Prophecy of Maitreya. Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has explained their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
May there be auspiciousness.
In the year 682, on the bright fortnight of Māgha,
on the day of the full moon, under the constellation Puṣya, on a Sunday, this was completed by Sarvānanda.
